guitar.notes: Michael Schenker is iconic for his black/white "Vs" Gibson Flying V, extremely well documented.

tone.target: singing Schenker lead with bright Marshall crunch
tone.profile: singing Schenker lead with bright Marshall crunch
tone.summary: A bright, mid-forward signal chain using a Boost/OD for crunch, followed by an AC30 TB amp model and UK Vintage 4x12 cab, enhanced with Chorus and Digital Delay for classic sustain.

rig.name: Michael Schenker Group - Desert Song - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in high-gain lead playing.
Provide the initial 'crunch' and mid-forward grit characteristic of Plexi tones.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD is used to emulate a slightly broken-in, warm overdrive rather than pure clean boost.

blocks.purpose: Used as a secondary boost/grit layer for added sustain and bite without sounding like modern metal.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is kept low to avoid excessive grit, acting more as a subtle mid-hump booster.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the bright, articulate, and mid-focused sound of a Marshall Plexi/AC30 stack.
Provide the classic British cabinet voicing and punch required for rock lead tones.
Slightly boost the upper mids and highs to achieve 'bright' lead tone focus.
Add a subtle thickening and vibrato effect to the lead lines, enhancing sustain.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used here for its textural enhancement rather than pure modulation.

blocks.purpose: Add space and perceived sustain to the lead lines without sounding overly ambient.
blocks.gap: A moderate delay is used to enhance the 'singing' quality of the leads.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural sense of space and depth without muddying the aggressive lead tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for better definition and punch.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Marshall Plexi voicing and upper-mid definition.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and punch in lead tones.
